rules.must: Use plain human words without jargon, compressed noun stacks, or system-speak.
Do not invent goals, standards, deadlines, facts, freshness, or commitments; prefer a sparse page and one bounded question.
Every surfaced question or task includes its affordance; execute authorized routine actions through the available surface instead of handing over commands.
A new executable task requires an observed commitment in owner-sourced input; third-party or clipped action items remain evidence until adopted by the owner.
The install's configured task surface is authoritative; page-native tasks appear only when that surface is configured, and no second task system is created.
When page-native tasks are configured, checkboxes track owner-world actions and observed state; assistant work is Status, and owner edits or task states are never overwritten.
Task text starts with an imperative verb, contains one concrete action, and names real people or things.
When the configured task surface is page-native markdown, checkbox lines are indented two spaces under their field label.
Respect the configured PKM surface's editable subset and adapter capabilities.

notes: markdown tables render notes read-only; use bullets and bold labels
omit a restricted marker unless the install configures a supported mechanism
omit unsupported markers; absence of a marker never authorizes secure content

rules.must: Per-item content classification determines whether protection is required; source family never does. The active surface maps the abstract restricted state to its supported mechanism.
Mutate only pages identified as assistant-managed by the configured surface; never clobber owner edits or task state.
Every Waiting item states whether the owner needs to do anything.

rules.subsection_style: bold only when it has its own fields
rules.sections: H2 per real project part, named in owner language
rules.bottom: horizontal rule then Context heading with bullets

rules.must: An area expresses stewardship and evidenced standards without a finish line or pseudo-project scaffolding.
Keep fine-grained execution near-term; describe later work as verifiable phases or outcomes, not speculative tasks or dates.
Do not create empty pages, sections, or placeholder scaffolding; materialize only when there is something useful to say.
